title: Land receipts from both wrappers and reconcile a crash between the ref move and the receipt
description:
Split out of task-b1c9850824fe4437a8c70b4ee083602b on 2026-09-12, applying the operator's earlier ruling that a card at the size gate's ceiling is split rather than planned whole. That card needed roughly twelve files across TypeScript and both launcher scripts. It keeps the daemon side: the DeliveryReceipt type, its store and the recording tool. This card owns the wrapper side, which is where acceptance criterion 6 actually lives.

Objective: make the landing itself prove where the code went, and make a crash between the ref move and the bookkeeping recoverable without landing twice.

Deliverable, in scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and scripts/moe-agent.sh with their harnesses:
- Every successful landing records a delivery receipt through the tool delivered by the prerequisite card, carrying the target name, the target revision before and after, the landed revision and the push result when the policy requires one.
- When the target revision moved between the check run and the landing, the wrapper reconstructs the candidate against the new tip and reruns the gate. A cached check result is reused ONLY when the candidate tree and the base both match exactly.
- Replaying a landing after a crash between the ref update and the receipt write reconciles to the landing that already happened and writes the one missing receipt, rather than moving the target a second time.

Unskips the acceptance case "a crash between an external effect and its bookkeeping does not repeat the effect" (src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts, describe at line 1982). That case executes the ACTUAL platform wrapper, generates its Codex and transport shims at runtime, routes every business call through the production McpAdapter, and kills the whole process tree while the receipt request is in flight. Its assertions may not be edited.

Not in scope: the receipt type, store and tool, which the prerequisite card delivers; batch or queued integration of several candidates, which is Wave 2.

Verification: npx vitest run src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts from packages/moe-daemon, then bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh from the repo root.
definitionOfDone: Both wrappers write a delivery receipt on every successful landing, carrying target before and after, the landed revision and the push result
A target that moved between check and landing forces a rebuilt candidate and a rerun gate; a cached result is reused only on an exact candidate tree and base match
Replaying the landing after a crash between the ref update and the receipt write reconciles to the existing landing and writes the one missing receipt, never moving the target twice
The acceptance case for a crash between effect and bookkeeping is unskipped and passes with no edit to its assertions
Wrapper string parity holds across both launchers and the postflight harness covers the new landing path
npx vitest run src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts passes, bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh passes, and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes
taskRails: Reconciliation must be idempotent: never land the same candidate twice after a crash.
The wrapper stays the only git actor; the daemon must not gain a git or process action from this card.
Wave 2 owns queued or batched integration; this card handles one candidate at a time.
Both launchers change together and parity-check must stay green.

implementationPlan.description:
Phases 1+2 — read the held-out case as the specification, capture baselines, no repo edits.

The spec is packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts, the describe at ~1981 and its fixtures at ~600-1010. Read them before touching a wrapper. What the case pins, and every number below is from the fixture, not from this plan:
- STRICT_SETTINGS: deliveryPolicy 'local-branch', autoCommit true, qualityGate 'node gate.cjs' with scope everyTask, consolidationBranch 'wave1-pilot', checkpointPush false. The pilot repo has NO remote.
- The wrapper runs with -CodexExec/--codex-exec, -NoStartDaemon, -NoLoop, -PollInterval 0, MOE_PROXY_PATH pointing at a generated transport shim, and the same -WorkerId in both runs.
- The transport holds the FIRST moe.record_delivery_receipt request forever. At that barrier: refs/heads/wave1-pilot already equals args.landedRevision, that commit's parent is base, the candidate file carries baseRevision=base and treeSha=the landed tree, exactly ONE check run is bound to it (command 'node gate.cjs', exitCode 0, source runner-observed) and .moe/receipts is EMPTY. So the receipt is sent after the ref move and after the ledger record, and it is the last daemon call of the landing.
- After the crash and the second run: the ref moved exactly once (reflog is [landed, base]), exactly one receipt exists with targetBefore=base, targetAfter=landedRevision=landed and pushResult=null, the candidate and check files are byte-identical, and there is exactly ONE attempt record, generation 1, phase closed. Run 2 therefore must not land, must not re-freeze, must not open an attempt, and must still close the one that is finalizing.

Re-read the wrapper anchors this card extends (both twins, by grep):
- sh: freeze_candidate, run_frozen_gate, land_plumbing, push_branch, record_commit_rpc, moe_evidence_rpc, baseline_path, preflight_landing, MOE_ATTEMPT_ID/MOE_ATTEMPT_GENERATION, FROZEN_CANDIDATE_ID/FROZEN_BASE_REVISION/FROZEN_TREE, GATE_CHECK_ID, LAND_PUSHED.
- ps1: Invoke-MoeLanding (its 3-attempt CAS loop), New-MoeFrozenCandidate, Invoke-MoeFrozenGate, Send-MoeCandidate, Send-MoeCheckRun, Send-MoeRecordCommit, Push-MoeBranch, Get-MoeBaselinePath, Invoke-MoeRecoveryCheck, Invoke-MoeIdleRecovery, $script:MoeFrozen, $script:MoeGate, $script:MoeAttemptId/$script:MoeAttemptGeneration.
- The receipt tool contract is docs/MCP_SERVER.md 'moe.record_delivery_receipt' plus comment-d779eb16 on this task: 40-hex revisions compared exactly, target ≤ 255 chars, pushResult a non-blank ≤ 2000-char string or null, no id (the daemon generates one), one receipt per candidate, an identical replay answers duplicate:true and writes nothing, a differing one is refused DELIVERY_RECEIPT_CONFLICT.

Baselines to record in the step note:
- `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts` today (criterion 6 still skipped).
- In a scratch copy of the test file with only `.skip` removed, run it once and capture the OLD-BEHAVIOUR failure the case demands as a counterexample: today no wrapper ever calls record_delivery_receipt, so run 1 exits and the case fails at the barrier. Quote that failure verbatim — it is the red proof for DoD 4.
- `MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh`, `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh`, and the ps1 twins launched from PowerShell (mem:gotcha-ps-harness-ctrlc-from-git-bash), with their frozen/scope counts.
- Note which acceptance half this box can actually run: on Windows the case drives moe-agent.ps1, so the sh twin's coverage has to come from postflight.sh arms.
implementationPlan.note:
Spec read (acceptance.test.ts:1981 + fixtures 600-1010); no repo edits. Baselines at HEAD 750c050:
- acceptance.test.ts: 4 passed | 2 skipped (6).
- RED counterexample (scratch copy D:/moe-bfe2-rcpt-397719, only .skip removed, today's ps1 wrapper): "Error: wrapper run 1 exited ({"code":0,"signal":null}) without calling moe.record_delivery_receipt: the receipt barrier was never reached" (5.6 s; run-1 RPC tail: record_candidate, record_check_run, chat_send[PUSH FAILED], record_commit, finalize_attempt, chat_send, deregister_worker).

Findings that change the plan's mechanics (recorded, not new scope):
1) Replay must run AFTER the pre-flight claim RPC, not before: if the attempt is finalized first, run 2's claim answers hasNext:false and the single-shot taskless wait (MOE_TASKLESS_WAIT_SEC default 300 s) blows the case's 300 s run-2 deadline. With the attempt still finalizing the claim is refused (ATTEMPT_FINALIZING) -> preflightClaimFailed -> no wait, no launch. Still independent of a successful claim, which was the plan's reason.
2) targetBefore = the CAS expected-old value: equals the frozen candidate's baseRevision on a born target, and git's zero oid on an unborn one (tool contract), not the empty-tree sentinel.
3) Wrappers hot-reload moe-agent.ps1 fleet-wide on edit, so all wrapper/harness work is done in the scratch tree and copied in whole after cmp against base/ (HEAD copy).
Incident: a duplicate wrapper (pid 46200, orphaned) ran a second CLI (session moes-2e) on this task; it stood down with zero repo edits and hard-killed its own wrapper; governor alerted (msg-a98f64c9).

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 3 — harness arms first, in scripts/tests/postflight.sh and scripts/tests/postflight.ps1. The embedded fake proxy and frozen suite are twins: every added line byte-identical in both files. Use the Edit tool (mem:gotcha-serena-edit-rewrites-crlf-on-windows, mem:gotcha-bash-tool-json-escapes-generated-code).

(a) Fake proxy: teach evidenceRpc about record_delivery_receipt, validating like the real tool rather than green-mocking it — 40-hex targetBefore/targetAfter/landedRevision, a non-blank target ≤ 255 chars, pushResult null or a non-blank string ≤ 2000 chars, the candidateId must name a recorded candidate, at most one receipt per candidate written to .moe/receipts/<id>.json, a byte-identical replay answering {duplicate:true} with no write, and a differing replay refused with DELIVERY_RECEIPT_CONFLICT. Keep the existing rpc log line so arms can assert ordering.

(b) New frozen modes (add to `modes`, keep the existing ones untouched):
- `receipt`: an ordinary gated completion. Asserts exactly one record_delivery_receipt, sent AFTER record_commit and BEFORE finalize_attempt, carrying candidateId = the recorded candidate, target = refs/heads/<branch>, targetBefore = that candidate's baseRevision, targetAfter = landedRevision = the new tip, pushResult null (the fixture repo has no remote), and that the receipt file exists.
- `receipt-manual` and `receipt-nogate`: autoCommit=false and a gate-less completion record NO receipt (there is no candidate to bind one to) and still land or skip exactly as today.
- `receipt-replay`: the crash. Drive it with the wrapper's own journal: run a gated completion with the receipt RPC failing (FAKE_EVIDENCE_MODE record_delivery_receipt-refuse or -null), which leaves the ref moved and the journal on disk; then run the wrapper again in the same fixture and assert the second run moves no ref (tip and reflog unchanged), records exactly one receipt with the SAME report bytes, opens no attempt, and deletes the journal.
- `receipt-race`: the target moves between the check run and the CAS (reuse the existing MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_HOOK_PRE_UPDATE_REF seam). Assert the rebuilt candidate is re-frozen against the new tip, the gate RERUNS (two check runs, the second bound to the new candidate and tree), and the receipt's targetBefore equals the SECOND candidate's baseRevision.
- `receipt-cached-check`: the CAS fails once but the tip is unchanged, so the rebuilt tree AND base match exactly. Assert the gate runs ONCE, the same candidate id is reused, and exactly one check run exists.

(c) Error handling in the arms: every assertion carries the captured wrapper log, a receipt RPC refusal must leave the landing committed (a refused receipt is bookkeeping, never a reason to roll back or re-land), and the journal must survive that refusal for the next run.

Prove each arm RED against today's wrappers before implementing (`MOE_FROZEN_TEST_ONLY=<mode>`, one run each, the ps1 twin launched from PowerShell), and record the first failing assertion per arm.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 4a — decide the push result, in both twins, because the receipt's pushResult field depends on it.

Rule: pushResult is null when no push was ATTEMPTED, and a bounded one-line summary when one was. So teach push_branch (sh ~4048) and Push-MoeBranch (ps1 ~3226) to return three outcomes instead of two: pushed, failed, or not-attempted.
- Not attempted when the repository has no remote at all (`git remote` prints nothing) — today both twins run `git push -u origin <branch>` against a repo with no origin, log two warnings and report pushed=false. The acceptance fixture is exactly that repo, and it requires pushResult null.
- Also not attempted on the paths that already skip a push (a checkpoint with settings.checkpointPush=false).
- When a push ran, build ONE line, at most 500 chars, from the outcome and the branch — for example `pushed refs/heads/<branch> to origin` or `push failed: <first stderr line, trimmed>`. Never raw push output: the tool REFUSES anything over 2000 chars rather than truncating it.

Keep the existing record_commit `pushed` boolean exactly as it is: a not-attempted push stays pushed=false, so no existing arm or delivery-policy check changes meaning. Add the no-remote notice as one `[info]` line, spelled identically in both twins.

Error handling: a `git remote` probe that fails for any reason is treated as 'remote unknown' and falls through to today's push attempt, so a probe failure can never silently stop pushing on a project that depends on it.
implementationPlan.note:
Push result, both twins (scratch tree; copied into the repo with the rest once green, because live seats hot-reload moe-agent.ps1):
- ps1 Push-MoeBranch / sh push_branch first probe `git remote`: rc 0 + empty output => no push attempted, one line `[info] no git remote configured; push skipped, the commit stays local on <branch>.` (identical text), result null ($script:MoePushResult / LAND_PUSH_RESULT empty), return false/1 so record_commit `pushed` stays false exactly as before. A failing probe falls through to today's push.
- pushed (first try or after rebase) => 'pushed <branch>'; failed => 'push failed: ' + the first trimmed ^(fatal|error): line of the last push output (else 'git push failed'), cut at 500 chars. PUSH FAILED / CHECKPOINT-UNPUSHED banners unchanged. sh run_landing resets LAND_PUSH_RESULT per landing.
Verified (sh from Git Bash, ps1 under powershell.exe; both parsers 0 errors): pass -> '[info] no git remote configured; push skipped...', receipt-push -> '[OK] Pushed task task-postflight to moe/frozen.', receipt-push-failed -> fatal: '...missing.git' does not appear to be a git repository + retry. All three still fail only at 'a landed gated candidate records exactly one delivery receipt' (step 4).

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 4b — the landing journal and the receipt call, in both twins. This is the durable-first pattern the epic already uses: persist the report that describes the effect BEFORE the effect, so a crash can replay the same report instead of recomputing one.

(a) Journal file, beside the existing per-task baseline: `<gitdir>/moe/receipt/<taskId>.json`, written with the same atomic temp-then-rename the baseline uses. Contents: taskId, workerId, attemptId, generation, candidateId, target, targetBefore, targetAfter, landedRevision, pushResult, and a state field.
- targetBefore is the FROZEN CANDIDATE's baseRevision (sh FROZEN_BASE_REVISION, ps1 $script:MoeFrozen.BaseRevision), never recomputed from the current tip: a recomputed value is exactly what makes a replay conflict, and it is already the empty-tree sentinel on an unborn target.
- target is the same string the candidate carries as deliveryTarget: `refs/heads/<branch>`.
- targetAfter and landedRevision are the commit-tree sha, known before update-ref.

(b) Write the journal immediately after the commit object exists and BEFORE update-ref (sh land_plumbing, ps1 Invoke-MoeLanding's CAS attempt loop), for gated completions only — a landing with no candidate has nothing to bind a receipt to. On a CAS failure the journal is rewritten by the next attempt (the ref never moved, so the stale report is safe to replace).

(c) After the CAS succeeds, keep today's order — index refresh, push, record_commit — then update the journal with the resolved pushResult and send `moe.record_delivery_receipt { candidateId, target, targetBefore, targetAfter, landedRevision, pushResult }` through the existing evidence-RPC helper (sh moe_evidence_rpc, ps1 the Send-MoeCandidate/Send-MoeCheckRun pattern), sending exactly the journaled bytes. Delete the journal when the call answers success, whether duplicate is true or false.

(d) Error handling, and it decides the whole card's safety:
- A refused or unanswered receipt NEVER rolls back, re-lands or fails the landing. The commit is on the branch; the landing outcome, the ledger row and the finalize outcome stay 'landed'.
- Log one `[WARN]` line naming the journal path and keep the journal for the next session to replay.
- DELIVERY_RECEIPT_CONFLICT is treated as already-recorded: log it, delete the journal, do not retry.
- A journal that cannot be written is also not fatal: log and continue — the landing must not be blocked by its bookkeeping, and the next session's recovery checkpoint still covers the bytes.

Arms `receipt`, `receipt-manual` and `receipt-nogate` from step 2 turn green.
implementationPlan.note:
Journal + receipt, both twins (scratch tree):
- Journal <gitdir>/moe/receipt/<taskId>.json (Get-MoeReceiptJournalPath / receipt_journal_path, same id whitelist as the baseline), atomic temp+rename, best-effort ([WARN] 'receipt journal not written (...); a crash before the receipt would leave this landing without one.'). Fields: taskId, workerId, attemptId, generation, candidateId, target, targetBefore, targetAfter, landedRevision, pushResult. No `state` field: whether the effect happened is asked of git at replay, a stored state could only disagree with it.
- Written for gated completions only, after commit-tree and immediately before update-ref. targetBefore = the CAS expected-old ($oldArg / ${old:-$MOE_ZERO_OID}), i.e. the landed candidate's baseRevision, zero oid when unborn. Initial pushResult = null when `git remote` is empty, else 'push result unknown: the landing stopped before its push finished' (so a crash between CAS and push never records a false 'no push'). A failed update-ref deletes that attempt's journal (the ref never moved).
- After CAS -> index refresh -> push -> record_commit (order unchanged): journal rewritten with the real pushResult, then Send-MoeReceipt / receipt_send sends exactly those fields (pushResult omitted when null) through the existing evidence helper (Send-MoeEvidence / moe_evidence_rpc now map record_delivery_receipt -> `receipt` and compare every sent key). Success (new or duplicate) deletes the journal; DELIVERY_RECEIPT_CONFLICT (ps1 $script:MoeRpcCodeName captured in Invoke-MoeRpc; sh grep of the captured stderr) is logged and treated as recorded; anything else logs '[WARN] delivery receipt not recorded for candidate <id>; journal kept at <path> for the next pre-flight to replay.' and never changes the landing, ledger row or finalize.
- Harness: +2 arms receipt-refused (journal kept verbatim, no receipt file, finalize still landed) and receipt-conflict (journal deleted, WARN, landing intact).
Verified, one run per mode, both engines (Git Bash sh; powershell.exe 5.1 from PowerShell): pass, race-pass, unborn, no-change, manual, disabled, receipt-push, receipt-push-failed, teardown-landed, finalize-loss-once, receipt-refused, receipt-conflict all PASS 1. RED of the 2 new arms on pristine wrappers (redtree/): receipt-refused 'a journal outlives its landing only while its receipt is unrecorded', receipt-conflict 'a landed gated candidate records exactly one delivery receipt'. Baseline sh frozen suite at HEAD: PASS 50.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 4c — reconcile a crash between the ref move and the receipt, in both twins. This is the half that makes run 2 of the acceptance case behave.

Hook: in the pre-flight, after the settings and git probe and BEFORE claim_next_task. It must not depend on holding a task — in the acceptance case the seat's own claim is refused with ATTEMPT_FINALIZING (it still holds the finalizing attempt), and a wrapper that reconciled only after a successful claim would never run.

For each `<gitdir>/moe/receipt/*.json` journal:
1. Read it; a malformed or unreadable journal is logged and SKIPPED, never thrown on and never deleted (a human can inspect it).
2. Ask git whether the effect happened: the journaled targetAfter is the target's tip, or an ancestor of it (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`). This tolerates peers landing on the shared branch afterwards.
3. Effect happened → send the journaled report verbatim, including its pushResult, and delete the journal on success or on DELIVERY_RECEIPT_CONFLICT. Do NOT re-land, do NOT re-freeze a candidate, do NOT re-run the gate, and do NOT touch the ref.
4. Effect did not happen (the ref never moved) → delete the journal and leave the bytes to the existing baseline recovery, which lands them as a checkpoint exactly as today.
5. Only when the journal's workerId equals THIS seat's worker id, and only after the receipt is recorded, close the boundary with the journaled attemptId and generation through the existing finalize ladder (outcome 'landed', landedRevision = the journaled one). A journal from another seat never has its attempt acknowledged — the wrapper rule is that a seat acknowledges only an identity IT pinned, and the journal is that pin made durable.

Idempotence, per the task rail: every branch above is safe to repeat — the ref check is a read, the receipt is idempotent by candidate, and the finalize is idempotent on a closed attempt.

Error handling: the whole scan is best-effort and bounded. Any failure logs one line and continues to the claim; it never aborts the pre-flight, never blocks the launch and never deletes a journal it could not act on.

Arm `receipt-replay` from step 2 turns green.
implementationPlan.note:
Replay, both twins (Invoke-MoeReceiptReplay / receipt_replay), scratch tree.
Hook: right AFTER the pre-flight claim_next_task RPC for every non-governor role, whatever the claim answered (deviation from 'before the claim', see step-1 note: closing the attempt first sends a single-shot run into the 300 s taskless wait; a still-finalizing attempt makes the claim refuse ATTEMPT_FINALIZING = no wait, no launch). Still independent of a successful claim.
Per <gitdir>/moe/receipt/*.json: malformed (name != taskId.json, bad ids, generation, 40-hex fields) -> '[WARN] receipt journal <f> kept: malformed journal', never deleted; task held by another LIVE session (Test-MoeLiveMarkerForeignLive / live_marker_foreign_live) -> skipped, so a peer's journal mid-landing is never raced; `git rev-parse -q --verify <target>^{commit}` + `merge-base --is-ancestor targetAfter tip` (ancestor, not equality: later peer landings still count; rc>1 or rev-parse rc>1 -> journal kept + WARN); not on target -> '[receipt] ... never moved the ref; dropping <f>' (baseline recovery owns the bytes); on target -> '[receipt] replaying the delivery receipt of task <id> from <f>', Send-MoeReceipt/receipt_send with the journal's own fields; then, only for journal.workerId == this seat and only while the journaled attempt file still reads finalizing for that id/task/generation (Get-MoePinnedAttemptPhase / moe_pinned_attempt_phase now take an optional identity), finalize_attempt outcome landed + journaled landedRevision via the existing evidence helper (3 tries). Never touches a ref, never re-freezes or re-gates. sh keeps MOE_TOP/MOE_GITDIR local so the pre-flight's probe is unchanged. Whole scan wrapped: a failure logs one line and continues to the claim flow.
Verified:
- receipt-replay PASS on sh (Git Bash) and ps1 (powershell.exe); pass, teardown-landed, finalizing-acked-continues still PASS on both.
- Acceptance case 6 (scratch copy, only .skip removed, REPO_ROOT = scratch so it drives the scratch moe-agent.ps1): 'Tests 1 passed | 5 skipped (6)', 7.5 s. Fixture RPC log (diagnostic write to a file in the scratch copy, restored + cmp'd after): run 1 ... record_candidate, record_check_run, record_commit, record_delivery_receipt -> HELD; run 2 ... claim_next_task -> refused -32002 ATTEMPT_FINALIZING, record_delivery_receipt -> ok, finalize_attempt -> ok, deregister_worker -> ok. So the attempt is closed by the replay, not by deregister's side effect.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 4d — a moved target rebuilds the candidate and reruns the gate; a cached result is reused only on an exact match. Both twins.

Today's CAS loop already rebuilds the tree and re-freezes when the branch moved under it, and the frozen gate runs again for the new candidate. This step makes that rule explicit and adds the ONE case where the gate may be skipped:
- Cache the gate result within the landing, keyed by the pair (candidate treeSha, candidate baseRevision) together with the candidate id and its check run.
- On a retry, reuse it ONLY when the rebuilt tree AND the base both equal the cached pair. Then the candidate is the same record — re-record the identical candidate (the tool answers duplicate:true and writes nothing) and keep its one check run; do not record a second check.
- Any other difference — a different base, a different tree, or either unknown — re-freezes a NEW candidate and REruns the gate, and its check run binds the new candidate and tree. A gate result from another tree or base is never evidence for this one.
- The receipt then reports the candidate that actually landed, whose baseRevision is the tip the CAS succeeded against.

Error handling: if the cached pair cannot be read back for any reason, fall through to the full re-freeze and rerun — the expensive path is the safe one, and a stale cache must never authorise a landing.

Arms `receipt-race` and `receipt-cached-check` from step 2 turn green. Re-run the existing race-pass/race-fail frozen arms: their candidate and check counts must not change.
implementationPlan.note:
Cached check, both twins (scratch tree). In the CAS loop, after the rebuilt tree is written: reuse ONLY when attempt > 1 AND the gated candidate of this landing exists (ps1 $script:MoeFrozen.CandidateId / sh FROZEN_CANDIDATE_ID + FROZEN_TREE) AND its tree AND base equal the rebuilt tree and current CAS base; then one '[info] qualityGate result reused: the rebuilt candidate has the same tree and base.' and no re-freeze, no second check. Anything else, or a pair that cannot be read back, re-freezes and reruns the gate as today. Reaching attempt 2 already implies attempt 1's gate passed (every gate/evidence failure returns). sh no longer clears FROZEN_* after a failed CAS (ps1 never did) so the pair survives to the next attempt. Deviation: the reused candidate is NOT re-recorded (the plan suggested a duplicate:true re-record): it carries no new information, and the finalizing hold means no claim can supersede the attempt between attempts.

comments.author: worker-62409c0c
comments.content:
CONTRACT NOTES FROM THE DAEMON HALF (task-b1c9850824fe4437a8c70b4ee083602b, going to REVIEW now), for whoever plans this wrapper half.

CALL:
- `moe.record_delivery_receipt { candidateId, target, targetBefore, targetAfter, landedRevision, pushResult? }`.
- There is no id: the daemon generates `receipt-<32 hex>`. The candidate is the key: at most one receipt per candidate, never rewritten.

INPUT RULES (refused, never coerced):
- Revisions must be exactly 40 hex. They are stored verbatim and compared exactly, case included.
- `target`: non-blank, unpadded, no control chars, at most 255 chars.
- `pushResult`: a non-blank string of at most 2000 chars, or null/omitted when no push was required (both are stored as null). Longer is REFUSED, not truncated, so send a bounded one-line summary, not raw push output.

ANSWER: `{ success: true, receipt, duplicate }`.
- `duplicate: false`: this call recorded the landing.
- `duplicate: true`: an identical receipt already existed and nothing was written. Read it as "already recorded", never as a reason to land again, and never infer either answer from the absence of an error.

A REPLAY MUST BE THE SAME REPORT. Any differing field is refused with `-32002`, `data.codeName` `DELIVERY_RECEIPT_CONFLICT`. The message names the differing fields; the error context does not cross the wire.
- So persist the report, especially `targetBefore`, BEFORE moving the ref.
- A `targetBefore` recomputed from the current tip after a crash WILL conflict.
- Criterion 6 projects `targetBefore: base` and replays `held.args` expecting one file with identical bytes, which the duplicate path satisfies.

OTHER REFUSALS:
- `-32002 DELIVERY_RECEIPT_AMBIGUOUS`: two receipts on disk for one candidate, which only hand-placed files cause.
- `-32001 CANDIDATE_NOT_FOUND`: checked only when no receipt exists yet, so a replay still reconciles when the candidate record is gone.
- `-32602 INVALID_INPUT` / `MISSING_REQUIRED`.
- A failed write is `-32000` with no receipt anywhere; retry the same report.

The daemon verifies nothing about the ref: a receipt is only what the wrapper reported.

comments.author: worker-d0c3b06e
comments.content:
Adversarial self-review (step 9), both twins.

1. Never twice, window by window:
- Before the journal (attribution, freeze, gate, commit-tree): no journal, ref unmoved. Next session: baseline recovery lands the bytes as a checkpoint, unchanged. The seat's finalizing attempt stays open, so its own claims are refused until a graceful exit deregisters. Pre-existing residual, not this card.
- Journal written, update-ref not done: the replay's `merge-base --is-ancestor` says no. One `[receipt] ... never moved the ref; dropping` line, journal deleted, then as above. A failed CAS inside the landing deletes its journal at once.
- update-ref done, record_commit not: the replay records the receipt from the journal. pushResult is null with no remote, else 'push result unknown: the landing stopped before its push finished'. It then closes the seat's own attempt as landed. RESIDUAL: the ledger row is still missing. A hard crash here always lost it; the replay does not re-send record_commit. Under strict local-branch policy, qa_approve will name completion-commit as missing. Follow-up: journal the sessionId and re-send a minimal record_commit in the replay (idempotent by sha). It is the longest window once a remote exists (the push).
- record_commit done, receipt not: this is the acceptance case (first receipt held, whole tree killed). Run 2's claim is refused ATTEMPT_FINALIZING. The replay records exactly one receipt and closes the attempt. Reflog stays [landed, base]. The harness twin is receipt-replay.
- Receipt persisted, answer lost: the replay re-sends identical bytes and gets duplicate:true. Journal deleted; finalize is idempotent on a closed attempt.

2. Replay fidelity: replay args are built only from the journal file (Send-MoeReceipt takes the parsed journal; receipt_send parses the journal JSON from stdin). Nothing is recomputed from git or settings. receipt-replay asserts the held and replayed calls are deepEqual. The acceptance case replays held.args and gets byte-identical storage. DELIVERY_RECEIPT_CONFLICT (ps1 via $script:MoeRpcCodeName, sh via a grep of the captured stderr) logs 'already has a delivery receipt that differs from this report', deletes the journal and never retries. Arm: receipt-conflict.

3. Concurrency: after a peer lands on top, my commit is still an ancestor of the tip, so the receipt is recorded. Equality would have dropped the journal and lost it. A `git revert` keeps my commit in history, so the receipt is still recorded. A force-reset that drops my commit makes the ancestor test fail, and the journal is dropped: that receipt would describe a landing that is no longer on the target. Ceiling: a pull --rebase retry inside my own push rewrites my commit. The receipt keeps the CAS move this wrapper made; record_commit keeps the rebased sha. Two seats replaying one journal: identical bytes, so one records and the other gets duplicate:true.

4. Foreign journals: the receipt is recorded; the attempt is never acknowledged. A seat may finalize only an identity it pinned, and the journal (workerId + attemptId + generation) is that pin made durable. Acknowledging someone else's attempt would lift the finalizing hold under a runner that may still be landing. Journals whose task a LIVE session holds (live marker) are skipped entirely, so a peer mid-push is never raced into a half-resolved pushResult.

5. No receipt and no journal for autoCommit=false, no-git or no-candidate paths. The general block asserts receipts.length 0 and an empty journal dir on every non-landed arm: manual, no-git, disabled, deferred, nogate-qa-claimed, no-change, all identity/evidence failures, all gate failures. The teardown arms assert it separately; teardown-landed deliberately keeps its journal.

6. Same tree, different base: arm receipt-same-tree-race. A peer lands an EMPTY commit before the CAS, so the rebuilt tree is byte-identical and only the base moved. Reusing the check would bind it to a candidate whose base never ran it, and required-check evidence keys on the current candidate. The rule requires tree AND base, so the arm sees 2 candidates, 2 checks and no 'reused' line. Dropping the base comparison makes that arm fail on both engines (actual 1 vs expected 2).

7. pushResult: null means no push was attempted. That is a different fact from a push that failed or said nothing, so both twins now skip the push when `git remote` is empty. A failed probe still pushes. The string is capped at one line of at most 500 chars, built from git's own fatal:/error: line, because the tool refuses anything over 2000 chars. Trusting it with raw push output would turn a push failure into a refused receipt and an orphaned journal.

8. The worst case would be a receipt for a landing that never happened, or a second landing after a crash. The first is prevented because git is asked before every replay and the report is never recomputed. The second is prevented because the replay path only reads git, sends one receipt and closes one attempt. The acceptance case pins the reflog at exactly [landed, base]; receipt-replay pins tip + reflog on both engines. Embarrassing but survivable: the missing ledger row in window 3, flagged above for a follow-up. Also considered: a planted journal with an odd target can only come from someone who can already write .git/hooks. Every field except target is shape-checked before it reaches git argv.

Parity green on both scripts (sh; ps1 under pwsh and 5.1). The guard was proven on a mutant. Repo files cmp-identical to the verified scratch files. No mutant or diagnostic leaked (grepped). Scratch tree removed after unlinking its node_modules junction.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
The held-out acceptance case is the specification, and it decides most of the design:
- The receipt is the LAST daemon call of a landing, after the ref move and the ledger row, because the barrier fires with the ref already moved, the candidate and check already bound, and .moe/receipts empty.
- targetBefore is the frozen candidate's baseRevision, never recomputed. The daemon refuses a differing replay, and a value recomputed from the tip after a crash is exactly what would differ (comment-d779eb16).
- Reconciliation is driven by a durable per-task journal beside the existing baseline, read in the pre-flight BEFORE the claim. Rejected: reconciling after a successful claim — in the acceptance case the seat's own claim is refused with ATTEMPT_FINALIZING, so that path never runs. Rejected: asking the daemon whether a receipt exists — the wrapper would still need the original report, and the journal is that report.
- Rejected: having the wrapper re-run the landing and rely on the CAS to no-op. The old-behaviour counterexample the case names is exactly a second post-base movement of the target.
- pushResult null comes from 'no push was attempted', which means teaching both twins that a repository with no remote needs no push. Rejected: tying pushResult to deliveryPolicy alone — a legacy project that really pushes would then report nothing.
- The cached check reuses a result only when tree AND base match, in which case the candidate is the same record and is re-recorded idempotently. A same-tree, different-base rebuild reruns the gate, because delivery policy binds a required check to the CURRENT candidate and its tree.
- Receipts are written only for landings that froze a candidate; the tool has no other binding, and a checkpoint or gate-less completion has none. Stated openly rather than stretched.

1. The acceptance case runs the REAL wrapper, kills a process tree and allows 720 s. Run it alone on a quiet box; a timeout there is a failure to diagnose, not a flake to retry blindly.
2. Its assertions may not be edited. Only `it.skip` and the stale UNSKIP OWNER comment change in that file.

completionSummary:
Both wrappers now record a delivery receipt for every landed gated candidate, and replay it after a crash without landing a second time.
- Journal: <gitdir>/moe/receipt/<taskId>.json, written atomically BEFORE update-ref. It holds the whole report: target, targetBefore = CAS base (zero oid if unborn), targetAfter = landedRevision, and pushResult. The pushResult starts as null with no remote, else as 'push result unknown…'. The journal is rewritten after the push.
- Sending: the receipt is the landing's last daemon call, after record_commit and before finalize. It goes through the existing evidence helpers. On success or DELIVERY_RECEIPT_CONFLICT the journal is deleted. A refusal or a lost answer only logs a WARN and keeps the journal; the landing, its ledger row and finalize are never touched.
- Replay: runs right AFTER the pre-flight claim, because a still-finalizing seat's claim is refused, which skips the 300 s single-shot wait. Journals whose task a live session holds are skipped. Git decides via merge-base --is-ancestor:
  - landed: the journaled bytes are resent verbatim, and the seat's OWN journaled attempt is closed as landed;
  - not landed: the journal is dropped.
  The replay never moves a ref, re-freezes or re-gates.
- Push: no `git remote` means no push attempt and pushResult null, with an [info] line. A pushed or failed push gives a bounded line of at most 500 chars. record_commit's `pushed` flag is unchanged.
- Gate reuse: a CAS retry reuses the passed gate only when tree AND base match. Same tree with a new base reruns the gate.
